title: First Position Not Smaller Than x

concept.title: Binary search for a boundary
body: With duplicates, "find x" is not precise enough. A cleaner question is: where is the **first** element that is `>= x`? In a sorted array the elements `< x` come first and the elements `>= x` after them, so we are looking for the border between the two groups.

Here `hi` is not excluded when `a[mid] >= x`, because `mid` itself may be the first such element. The loop ends with `lo == hi`, which is the border. This "lower bound" is the building block for counting equal values and for many later problems.

statement: You are given an array of `n` integers sorted in non-decreasing order (duplicates are possible) and `q` numbers `x`. For each `x` print the smallest index `i` (counting from 0) with `a[i] >= x`. If every element is smaller than `x`, print `n`.
inputFormat: The second line has the sorted array.
The third line has the `q` numbers `x`.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines, one answer per number.

examples.note: The answers: first 2 is at index 1; first value >= 3 is 5 at index 4; 0 gives index 0; 10 gives 6 = n.

hints: Look for the border between the elements smaller than x and the others.
Use `lo = 0`, `hi = n` and the loop `while lo < hi`.
If `a[mid] < x` set `lo = mid + 1`, otherwise set `hi = mid`.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
x = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: The array is a block of values `< x` followed by a block of values `>= x`. Binary search narrows `[lo, hi]` to the border between the blocks.
solution.complexity: Time O(q log n), space O(1) besides the input.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
x = list(map(int, input().split()))

out = []
for v in x:
    lo, hi = 0, n
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if a[mid] < v:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid
    out.append(lo)
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
